categories.main_business_segments: AECOM operates through three reportable segments: Americas (planning, consulting, architectural and engineering design, construction and program management services in the US, Canada, and Latin America), International (similar services in Europe, Middle East, India, Africa, and Asia-Australia-Pacific regions), and AECOM Capital (real estate investment and development). The company is a leading global provider of professional infrastructure consulting services across major end markets including transportation, facilities, water, environmental, and energy.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company delivers services primarily through fee-based knowledge services utilizing technical expertise in civil engineering, structural engineering, process engineering, mechanical engineering, geotechnical systems, electrical engineering, architectural design, landscape and interior design, and urban planning. Core methods include advisory services, planning, consulting, architectural and engineering design, construction management, and program management. The company is investing in digital capabilities and platforms to improve delivery efficiency and create innovative solutions for complex challenges.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers include national, state, regional and local governments (43% of fiscal 2023 revenue), and private entities worldwide (57% of revenue). Major end markets served are transportation (including transit, rail, marine ports, highways, bridges, tunnels, and aviation), facilities (green facilities, government, industrial, urban master planning, commercial, educational, healthcare, and sports), water (treatment, supply, resources, drought response, and hazardous chemicals), environment (management, remediation, permitting), and new energy (demand-side management, transmission, renewable energy, hydropower, and solar).
categories.geographic_coverage: AECOM operates globally with significant presence in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Europe, Middle East, India, Africa, and Asia-Australia-Pacific regions. Approximately 29% of fiscal 2023 revenue was attributable to services provided outside the United States to non-US clients. The company has approximately 52,000 employees worldwide, with approximately 18,000 in the United States, and operates through approximately 9,000 square feet of corporate offices in Dallas, Texas, plus approximately 6.4 million square feet of other offices globally.
categories.supply_chain_position: AECOM operates primarily as a service provider in the midstream and downstream portions of infrastructure project lifecycles, providing planning, design, management, and advisory services rather than manufacturing or construction execution. The company routinely subcontracts for services and incurs direct costs on behalf of clients, which are passed through as pass-through revenues (53% of total revenue in fiscal 2023). The company has exited substantially all self-perform at-risk construction businesses to focus on professional services.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include setting a new standard of excellence in professional services through greater connectivity and collaboration across regions and business lines, prioritizing core markets, and leveraging greatest strengths. The company is transforming work delivery through technology and digital platforms to improve client experience and efficiency. Key focus areas include building digital capabilities, capturing value from data libraries for efficient design processes, and developing innovative solutions for complex challenges. The company is also focused on ESG leadership, with net zero emissions reduction targets approved by the Science Based Targets Initiative, including 50% reduction by 2030 and 90% by 2040.
categories.revenue_model: AECOM generates revenue primarily through fee-based professional services billed on time-and-materials, cost-reimbursable, guaranteed maximum price, and fixed-price contract bases. For fiscal 2023, revenue composition was 43% cost-reimbursable, 34% guaranteed maximum price, and 23% fixed-price contracts. Revenue is recognized over time as performance obligations are satisfied, measured using an input method of total costs incurred divided by total costs expected. AECOM Capital derives income from real estate development sales and management fees. The company also generates revenue through equity earnings from unconsolidated joint ventures.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: AECOM is the second largest general architectural and engineering design firm in the world by 2022 design revenue according to Engineering News-Record's 2023 Design Survey. The company is ranked number one in transportation design, facilities design, environmental engineering, environmental consulting, and environmental science globally. The company competes with numerous regional, national, and international firms ranging from small private firms to multi-billion dollar companies. Competitive advantages include reputation, cost effectiveness, long-term client relationships, extensive office network, employee expertise, broad service range, and investments in technology and innovation.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: AECOM is a large accelerated filer with fiscal 2023 revenue of $14,378.5 million, representing 9.4% growth from fiscal 2022 revenue of $13,148.2 million. Gross profit increased 11.5% to $945.5 million. Net income attributable to AECOM was $55.3 million in fiscal 2023 compared to $310.6 million in fiscal 2022, impacted by $307.0 million impairment charge related to AECOM Capital investments. The company had approximately $1,262.2 million in cash and cash equivalents at September 30, 2023, and total debt of $2,217.3 million. Market capitalization was approximately $11.7 billion as of March 31, 2023.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: AECOM differentiates through market-leading technical capabilities, scale, and expertise in delivering innovative solutions for complex infrastructure challenges. The company emphasizes its ability to provide comprehensive services across project lifecycles, from planning and design through program management. Key differentiators include proprietary innovations such as the DE-FLUORO water treatment solution for PFAS contamination, leadership in ESG and sustainability initiatives, digital transformation capabilities, and a global network enabling localized knowledge combined with worldwide professional resources. The company positions itself as uniquely well-suited to address clients' Environmental, Social, and Governance objectives with focus on sustainability and resilience initiatives.
